manifest.intent: Test whether the reviewed semantic crawler SDF program recovers materially different donors inside one low-crawler morphology basin.

donors.visualSelectionRationale: Longest admitted crawler with repeated dorsal segmentation, a projected anterior tube, a low belly, and a relatively narrow contact footprint; this is the strongest axial-extent and segmentation challenge in the set.
Compact rounded crawler with concentrated anterior mass, a domed dorsal ridge, and a nearly circular posterior lobe; this challenges length reduction and front-to-back mass concentration.
Taller-backed crawler with a narrow front view, strong shell pressure, and a distinct tapered posterior appendage; this supplies the vertical-mass and silhouette-taper challenge.
Broad low crawler with paired posterior masses and a shallow dorsal arc; retained as the already-proven control and the widest lateral/contact-footprint member of the set.

visualInspection.visibleDelta: Across all four precommitted crawler donors, fitted silhouettes and depth volumes visibly approach donor body length, lateral and vertical mass, posterior taper, stance, and coarse contact footprint in all eight exact-camera rows, including the four diagonal held-out views. Donor-specific appendages, shell segmentation, and the Basin 03 anterior tube remain outside the current 13-parameter vocabulary.
